title: Vertical vs horizontal scaling

kcs.statement: Vertical scaling (scaling up) makes a single server bigger, with more CPU or memory; it is limited by the largest available machine and is common for non-distributed systems such as a database.
Horizontal scaling (scaling out) adds more servers that share the load; it needs a distributed application and is how web tiers usually scale in the cloud.

problem_ideas: A database server hits 95% memory: does moving from 16 GB to 64 GB RAM scale up or out?
A web shop goes from 2 to 10 identical web servers for Black Friday: name the scaling direction.
Which approach hits a hard ceiling, and why?
Pick the scaling type a call-centre analogy describes: hiring more operators versus training one operator to work faster.
A legacy app keeps session state on one machine: which scaling type is easiest and why?
Order three changes (bigger instance, more instances, add a load balancer) by which ones need a distributed app.
